en: The Sūtra on the Seven Buddhas Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Scattered Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Teaching, Dharma Deva, in accordance with the Imperial Edict.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, there was a great assembly of bhikṣus who, having taken their bowls, went to the Kāliṅga shrine at mealtime and sat together in contemplation.
"What Buddhas appeared in past ages, what were their clans and lifespans, and what was the significance of these matters?
Having reflected thus, they questioned one another but were unable to know.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing that this bhikṣu was contemplating these matters, rose from his seat, went to the Kāliṅga Grove, and sat down cross-legged.
At that time, the bhikṣus prostrated with their heads at his feet, stood to one side, and with palms joined in reverence, gazed up at him with single-minded devotion.
The World-Honored One asked them: "Bhikṣus, what do you think?"
The bhikṣus replied,
“We have reflected upon which Buddhas appeared in the past world,
yet we are unable to know their clans, their lineages, or their lifespans.”
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"Do you wish to hear?
The bhikṣus replied: "We do."
"Now is precisely the right time; we pray that you will expound it for us.
The Buddha said, "Listen attentively, and I shall now speak of it."
Ninety-one eons ago, the Buddha Vipaśyin, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, appeared in the world.
Thirty-one eons ago, the Buddha Śikhin and the Buddha Viśvabhū, both Arhats and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, appeared in the world.
In the sixth eon of the Bhadrakalpa, there appeared in the world the Buddha Krakucchanda, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha.
In the seventh eon, there appeared in the world the Buddha Kanakamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha.
In the eighth kalpa, there appeared in the world the Buddha Kāśyapa, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
In the ninth kalpa, I, Śākyamuni Buddha, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, appeared in the world.
Furthermore, in past kalpas, the Buddhas Vipaśyin, Śikhin, and Viśvabhū proclaimed the purity of śīla and the vinaya, thereby accomplishing the supreme practice of wisdom.
"Furthermore, during this Bhadrakalpa, the Buddhas Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, and Kāśyapa also taught the Dharma of pure discipline, meditative concentration, and liberation;
the Dharma I teach is likewise the same."
"O Bhikṣus! In the past, the Buddha Vipaśyin, born of the Kṣatriya caste, gave rise to pure faith and sought to leave the household life, thereby attaining the path of perfect enlightenment."
The Buddhas Śikhin and Viśvabhū were also of the Kṣatriya caste.
The Buddhas Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, and Kāśyapa were of the Brāhmaṇa caste.
"I was born in the palace of King Śuddhodana, of the Kṣatriya caste.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke in verse:
"In the past, throughout ninety-one kalpas, I have spoken."
At that time, Vipaśyin appeared in the world. Within thirty-one eons, Śikhin and Viśvabhū—
these Perfectly Awakened Ones— were all of the Kṣatriya caste.
The Tathāgata Krakucchanda was of the Brahmin caste;
Kanakamuni and Kāśyapa were likewise of that same lineage.
Now I dwell in Jambudvīpa as the son of Śuddhodana.
"Though he has realized the Buddha’s bodhi, his clan is still Kṣatriya.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying: "Listen attentively!
I shall now further declare the clan names of the seven Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas: the Buddhas Vipaśyin, Śikhin, and Viśvabhū were of the Kauṇḍinya clan.
The Buddha Krakucchanda, the Buddha Kanakamuni, and the Buddha Kāśyapa belonged to the Kāśyapa clan.
The Tathāgata Śākyamuni belongs to the Gautama clan.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
“Vipaśyin Tathāgata, Śikhin, and Viśvabhū— these three Buddhas were all of the Kauṇḍinya clan.”
K Krakucchanda Tathāgata, Kanakamuni, and Kāśyapa— these three Buddhas were all of the Kāśyapa clan. I,
dwelling in the realm of Jambudvīpa, was born in the palace of Śuddhodana.
"Having left the household life, he realized enlightenment; such is that one of the Gautama clan.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying: "Listen attentively!
I shall now further explain the length of the lifespans of the seven Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
When the Buddha Vipaśyin, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, appeared in the world, his lifespan was eighty thousand years.
The Buddha Śikhin, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Awakened One, appeared in the world with a lifespan of seventy thousand years.
The Buddha Viśvabhū, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Awakened One, appeared in the world with a lifespan of sixty thousand years.
The Buddha Krakucchanda, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, appeared in the world with a lifespan of forty thousand years.
The Buddha Kanakamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, appeared in the world with a lifespan of thirty thousand years.
The Buddha Kāśyapa, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, appeared in the world with a lifespan of twenty thousand years;
I, however, transform sentient beings of the five turbidities, whose lifespan is but one hundred years.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
“Vipaśyin Tathāgata, Śikhin, Viśvabhū, the World-Honored One Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, and Kāśyapa— ”
When these Buddhas appeared in the world, the respective lifespans of humanity were eighty thousand years,
then seventy thousand, sixty thousand, forty thousand,
thirty thousand, down to twenty thousand; such was the case for Śākyamuni Buddha.
"And having emerged from the five corruptions, the human lifespan shall be one hundred years.
At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken this verse, he addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively!
I shall now further speak of the various names of the parents, kingdoms, and cities of the seven Tathāgatas.
As for Vipaśyin Buddha, his father was named King Pūrṇamāyā, his mother was named Pūrṇamāyā, and the capital city was also named Pūrṇamāyā.
The Tathāgata Śikhin’s father was named King Aruṇa, his mother was also named Aruṇā, and the city was named Aruṣvatī.
The Tathāgata Viśvabhū’s father was named King Supratiṣṭhita, his mother was named Prabhāvatī, and the city was named Anupama.
As for Buddha Krakucchanda, his father’s name was Vipaśyanānta, his mother’s name was Viśākha, the king’s name was Kṣema-kṣama, and the city was named Kṣema.
The father of Krakucchanda Buddha was named Vainya-datta; his mother was named Udārā; the king was named Śubha; and the city was named Śobhāvatī.
The Tathāgata Kāśyapa’s father was named Sumedhas, his mother was named Mṛgāvatī, the king was named Kṛkin, and the city was named Vārāṇasī.
"I am now the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; my father’s name is King Śuddhodana, my mother’s name is Mahāmāyā, and the city is named Kapilavastu.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
"Vipaśyin Tathāgata— That Buddha’s original place of birth..."
Māndhātṛ was his father, and Māndhātṛvatī was his mother;
the great capital city where he resided was also named Māndhātṛ.
At that time, the country was abundant and prosperous, and the people were constantly happy.
The World-Honored One Śikhin, whose father was King Aruṇa and whose mother was named Aruṇavatī—
the city where he resided was likewise called Aruṇavatī.
The people were exceedingly numerous, Greatly wealthy and always at peace.
As for the Tathāgata Viśvabhū, His father, the king, and his mother’s names were Subhadratīrtha and Prabhāvatī.
The capital city of that realm was named Anupama;
its world was likewise peaceful and secure, free from all calamities.
The name by which the World-Honored One Krakucchanda was known was established by his father.
Yaneyaṇata, with Viśākha as his mother, was King Kṣema; he resided in the city of Kṣemā.
At that time, all those sentient beings revered and honored the virtuous and good.
Kunālamuni was born; his father’s name was Vyāghra and his mother’s name was Udārā;
the king’s name was Śubha, and the city was Śubhavatī.
Extensive and adorned with many ornaments, sentient beings were free from all afflictions.
Kāśyapa Buddha’s father was Sumedhas; his mother was Mṛgāvatī; his son was named Mahābhuja.
The King of Kṛki reigned with his capital at the city of Vārāṇasī;
all the sentient beings therein were always peaceful and secure day and night.
As for my current place of birth, King Śuddhodana is my father.
The mother was Mahāmāyā, and the city was named Kapilavastu.
Such are the names of the parents, the countries, and the cities of these seven Tathāgatas, the Perfectly Awakened Ones, as they are distinguished.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively!
I shall now further speak of the śrāvaka disciples of the seven Tathāgatas."
The great wise disciple of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vipaśyin was named Khaṇḍaśrī; he was the foremost among the śrāvakas.
The great wise disciple of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śikhin was named Trivikrama; he was the foremost among the śrāvakas.
The great wise disciple of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Viśvabhū was named Yaśodara, foremost among the śrāvakas.
The great wise disciple of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Krakucchanda was named Sanjīva, foremost among the śrāvakas.
The disciple of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Konāgamana, named Surūnudhara, was the foremost among the śrāvakas in great wisdom.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kāśyapa had a disciple of great wisdom named Bharadvāja, who was the foremost among the śrāvakas.
I, the present Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, have a disciple of great wisdom named Śāriputra, who is the foremost among the śrāvakas.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
"Vipaśyin Tathāgata had a son of great wisdom named Khaṇḍaśrī."
The World-Honored One Śikhin had a son of great wisdom named Trivikrama.
The Tathāgata Viśvabhū had a son of great wisdom named Yaśodharā.
The Tathāgata Krakucchanda had a son of great wisdom named Sanjīva;
the Tathāgata Kanakamuni had a son of great wisdom named Surūndhara.
The World-Honored One Kāśyapa Buddha had a son of great wisdom, Varatīrtha.
I, the present Arhat and Perfectly Enlightened One, have a son of great wisdom named Śāriputra.
"Thus, among all the śrāvakas, these seven sons of the Buddha are each the foremost.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively!
I shall now further speak of the attendant disciples of the seven Tathāgatas.
The attendant of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vipaśyin was named Aśoka.
The attendant of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śikhin was named Kṣemaka.
The attendant of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Viśvabhū was named Upaśānta.
The attendant of the Buddha Krakucchanda, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, was named Metreyu.
The attendant of the Buddha Kanakamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, was named Surudatya.
The attendant of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kāśyapa was named Sarvamideva;
my attendant now, as the Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, is named Ānanda.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
“The Buddha’s son Aśoka, Kṣemaka, Aruṇa, and others, Along with Upasānta And Maitreya.”
Suruditya, Sarvamitra, and Ānanda— each served as an attendant to the Buddha.
Constantly practicing a mind of loving-kindness and compassion, they accomplished samādhi.
Thoroughly penetrating the characteristics of all phenomena, Possessing great wisdom,
learned and sagacious, He is a teacher of the Great Dharma,
foremost among the assembly, His fame resounding throughout the ten directions.
Both humans and devas alike pay him homage; with the power of diligence firm and steadfast, he has severed all afflictions and realized the state beyond birth and death.
Having attended upon the Buddha, the World-Honored One, he constantly attains his own benefit.
"Such as these are the Tathāgatas, who have accomplished the state of true sons of the Buddha.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying: "Listen attentively!
I shall now further explain the assemblies of śrāvakas delivered by the Tathāgatas of the seven Buddhas.

At the first assembly when Vipaśyin Tathāgata preached the Dharma, sixty-two thousand bhikṣus attained the fruit of arhatship; at the second assembly when he preached the Dharma, one hundred thousand bhikṣus attained the fruit of arhatship; and at the third assembly when he preached the Dharma, eighty thousand bhikṣus attained the fruit of arhatship.

When Śikhin Tathāgata preached the Dharma at his first assembly, one hundred thousand bhikṣus attained the fruit of arhatship; at his second assembly, eight billion bhikṣus attained the fruit of arhatship; and at his third assembly, seventy thousand bhikṣus attained the fruit of arhatship.

When Vipaśyin Tathāgata preached the Dharma at his first assembly, eighty thousand bhikṣus attained the fruit of arhatship; at his second assembly, seventy thousand bhikṣus attained the fruit of arhatship; and at his third assembly, sixty thousand bhikṣus attained the fruit of arhatship.
“During a single assembly for preaching the Dharma, Krakucchanda Tathāgata caused forty thousand bhikṣus to attain arhatship.
During a single assembly for preaching the Dharma, Kanakamuni Buddha caused thirty thousand bhikṣus to attain the fruit of arhatship.”
When the Tathāgata Kāśyapa preached the Dharma in a single assembly, twenty thousand bhikṣus attained the fruit of arhatship.
Now, when I preach the Dharma in a single assembly, one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus have attained the fruit of arhatship.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
“Vipaśyin Tathāgata, Śikhin, Viśvabhū, the World-Honored One Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, and Kāśyapa.”
And Śākyamuni, each appearing in the world at their respective times,
the number of śrāvaka disciples they delivered was seventy billion,
ninety thousand, three hundred, and two hundred and fifty.
"All have attained arhatship, and shall not undergo further existence.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively!

From Vipaśyin Buddha, Śikhin Buddha, and Viśvabhū Buddha, up until my own appearance in this world, where I abide to sustain and transform beings, proclaiming the Dharma teachings to subdue sentient beings—there has not been the slightest difference in the precepts, conduct, and protocols, nor in the receiving and maintaining of robes and bowls, nor in the seeking of realization of Bodhi.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"In this manner, throughout past and present kalpas,
the bhikṣus delivered by Buddhas such as Vipaśyin have achieved great wisdom."
Diligently cultivate the true path, the factors conducive to enlightenment:
the five faculties and the five powers, the four foundations of mindfulness,
the four bases of psychic power, the seven factors of awakening, the eightfold noble path, and those samādhis.
With senses such as the eyes stilled, they penetrate the treasury of the Dharma;
awakening all living beings, they cause the life-force of wisdom to increase.
Thus, within this Bhadrakalpa, all praise them as unprecedented.
"By means of great compassion and wisdom, the Buddha has awakened himself and awakened others;
with majestic power and great supernormal faculties, all that he speaks is thus.

At that time, having spoken these verses, the World-Honored One rose from his seat together with the bhikṣus and returned to the Anāthapiṇḍada Park. When this night had passed, it was the time of dawn.
The assembly of bhikṣus went from their respective residences to the Kāliṅga shrine, where they questioned one another:
"The Tathāgatas of the past entered great parinirvāṇa, transcended all conceptual proliferation, forever severed the cycle of saṃsāra, and were free from all faults."

Such a Great Being, possessing such wisdom, such ethical discipline, such samādhi, such liberation, such majestic power, and such lineage, appearing in the world to benefit sentient beings, is truly rare and inconceivable.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the bhikṣus, rose from his seat, went to the Kālika Grove, sat down cross-legged, and addressed the assembly of bhikṣus:
"What do you think?"
Then the bhikṣus addressed the World-Honored One, saying:

“We have heard it said that the Tathāgatas of the past entered great parinirvāṇa, transcended all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and forever severed the cycle of saṃsāra; they were without fault, such great beings possessing such wisdom, such ethical discipline, such samādhi, such liberation, such majestic power, and such lineage, descending into the world to benefit living beings—this is truly rare and inconceivable.”
The Buddha said,
“Bhikṣu, for what reason do you now say this? The bhikṣu replied:
“The Buddha possesses the pure dharma-realm and has realized the wisdom of true awakening; there is nothing he does not know.
We pray that you will explain this for us. The Buddha said: “Bhikṣus, listen attentively; I shall now speak of it.”
In a past age, there was a great king named Mandhātṛ, and his queen was named Mandhātrī.

At that time, Vipaśyin Buddha descended from Tuṣita Heaven to Jambudvīpa and entered his mother’s womb to dwell within the embryonic treasury. He emitted a great radiance that illuminated all worlds, leaving no place in darkness; even those evil realms and all the hells, which the majestic light of the sun and moon could not reach, suddenly became brightly lit by the Buddha’s light. The sentient beings therein were able to see one another for the first time and cried out: "Why is it that there are other beings here?"
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva descends from Tuṣita to Jambudvīpa,
Like a cloud and like the wind, In an instant he enters his mother’s womb."
The body emits a great radiance, Illuminating the realms of humans and devas;
The hells and the Iron Ring Mountains Are all entirely freed from darkness.
Throughout the various spheres of the Buddha-fields, He dwells accordingly within the mother’s body.
"Such a multitude of great sages has likewise come together in this assembly.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen now with close attention!"
When that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva descended from Tuṣita Heaven to Jambudvīpa and entered his mother’s womb, the yakṣa Pūrṇamāya cried out in a loud voice:
"This Great Bodhisattva, a Great Being of majestic virtue, has relinquished his celestial body and his asura body to dwell within his mother’s womb and receive a human body."
Thus, when the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, and even up to the Brahmā-purohita Heaven heard this proclamation:
"The Bodhisattva has descended his spirit and entered the mother’s womb."
"All have now gathered.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva descended from Tuṣita, Entering the mother’s womb, his spirit was manifest."
The Great Yakṣa Pūrṇabhadra proclaimed: "That Bodhisattva has cast off his celestial body as well as his Asura form;
now dwelling within this mother’s womb, he receives the retribution of the human world."
The Four Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, Yāma and Tuṣita,
even up to the Brahma world— all have heard this news:
that the Bodhisattva has descended into the human realm, with a subtle and true golden hue.
"The devas have all gathered together, their hearts filled with great joy and celebration.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus:
"Listen now with close attention!

When that Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva descends from Tuṣita Heaven to Jambudvīpa, there are four great deva-sons endowed with majestic power, clad in armor and holding bows and swords in their hands, who protect the Bodhisattva so that neither humans nor non-humans can cause him harm.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva descended into birth, Śakra, Lord of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven,
dispatched the Four Heavenly Kings, each endowed with great majestic power."
Clad in golden armor and holding bows, swords, and spears in hand,
they provide constant protection at all times;
thus, rākṣasas and non-human beings do not dare to cause harm or affliction.
"Dwelling within the mother’s womb, as if staying in a great palace, one constantly experiences all manner of happiness.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen now with careful attention!"

When that Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva descends from Tuṣita Heaven to enter his mother’s womb in Jambudvīpa, his body is pure and radiates brilliant light like a maṇi jewel; his mother’s mind is peaceful and free from all feverish distress.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva dwells in the womb, He is pure and free from blemish;
Like a lapis lazuli bead, And also like a maṇi jewel."
His radiance illuminates the world, like the sun emerging from the clouds;
he has accomplished the ultimate truth and given birth to the supreme wisdom.
He causes his mother to be free from sorrow and affliction, and she constantly performs all manner of wholesome deeds.
"Sentient beings all look up to him, He dwells securely as a kṣatriya.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen now with close attention!"

When that bodhisattva-mahāsattva descended from Tuṣita Heaven to enter his mother’s womb in Jambudvīpa, his mother had never before experienced attachment to the five sensory objects, such as forms associated with defiled desire.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva dwells in the womb, he causes the mother’s mind to be pure;
she hears not the name of defilement and remains far removed from the faults of the five desires."
“Having severed the root of craving, one does not undergo various sufferings and afflictions;
body and mind are ever peaceful and secure, and one constantly attains happiness.
When the World-Honored One had spoken this verse, he addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively now!
When that Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva descended from Tuṣita Heaven to enter his mother’s womb in Jambudvīpa, his mother personally observed the five precepts of a lay follower (*upāsaka*):

first, not killing; second, not stealing; third, no sexual misconduct; fourth, not lying; and fifth, not drinking intoxicants. He was born from her right side as a Bodhisattva, and after his birth, she passed away and was reborn in the heavenly realms."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva dwells within the womb, the mother herself observes the five precepts;
a youth is born from her right flank, free from all such sufferings and afflictions."
"Just as Śakra, Lord of the Devas, Experiences the exquisite pleasures of the five desires,
When his life later comes to an end, He swiftly attains rebirth in the heavens.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus:
"Listen attentively now!

When that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva was born from the right side, the great earth shook; his body was of true golden color, free from all defilements, and he emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated all realms of the world. All the dark hells of the evil destinies were suddenly filled with light, and the sentient beings therein were able to see one another for the first time, each wondering:
'Why are there other sentient beings here?'"
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva was born, the great earth shook;
his physical marks were like pure gold, untainted by any dust or defilement."
"With majestic power and great supernormal faculties, their radiance illuminates all;
those sentient beings obscured by karma are thus able to see one another.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus:
"Listen attentively now!
When that Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva was born from the right side, his mother felt no fatigue; she neither sat nor lay down.
At that time, the Bodhisattva, a Great Being of majestic virtue, was not mentally obscured, and his feet did not touch the ground as four great deva-kings supported the body of the infant."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva descended into birth, The mother’s mind was free from distraction;
Neither sitting nor lying down, She remained at ease and full of joy."
“A majestic and powerful Great Being, whose mind is free from all obscurity—
the Four Heavenly Kings support his body, and his feet do not tread upon the earth.
When the World-Honored One had spoken this verse, he addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively now!

When that Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva was born from the right side, his body was pure like lapis lazuli, free from all impurities such as pus, blood, mucus, and saliva; it was just like a maṇi jewel or a Kauśika garment, upon which no dust or grime could adhere."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva descends into birth, His physical vessel is entirely pure;
He is far removed from all filth and evil, Such as pus, blood, mucus, and saliva."
"Just as a Kauśeya garment, And likewise a mani jewel,
With a body so pure and radiant, Dust and grime cannot abide upon it.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus:
"Listen attentively!
When that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva was born from the right side, two devaputras descended from the midst of the sky with two kinds of water—one cool and one warm—to bathe the youth."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva was born, Two devas in the sky bathed the child’s body, Causing two kinds of water to descend."
"Warmth and cold are each appropriate; manifesting the perfection of merit and wisdom, one achieves great fearlessness and gazes universally upon all sentient beings.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively now!

When that Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva was born from the right side, he was endowed with the thirty-two marks; his physical form was upright and majestic, and his faculty of sight was pure, seeing for ten yojanas."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the Bodhisattva descended into birth, All his marks were fully complete;
His eyes were pure and most dignified, Seeing clearly for ten yojanas."
At that time, having spoken these verses, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus:

"When that bodhisattva-mahāsattva was born from the right side, he beheld the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven. Śakra, Lord of the Devas, seeing that this child was the body of a true Buddha, held a white parasol over the child’s body, so that cold, heat, wind, dust, and all manner of evils could not invade him."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the youth was first born, he gazed afar at the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven;
Śakra, in turn, beheld him, holding a white parasol in his hand."
"It immediately comes to cover his body, so that cold, heat, wind, sun,
and all such poisonous evils cannot invade him at all.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively now!

When that Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva was born from the right side, his biological mother, foster mother, nurse, and all the palace attendants surrounded and protected him, bathing him, anointing him with fragrant scents, and attending to him in every way."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the youth was first born, Three nurses and the palace attendants Constantly surrounded him on all four sides."
"Bathed and further anointed with fragrant perfumes, may they always be secure;
thus, throughout day and night, may I never for a moment abandon them.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus:
"Listen attentively now!
When that Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva was born from his mother’s right side, his body was majestic and beautiful, endowed with the thirty-two marks.
King Pūrṇadruma immediately summoned a physiognomist to examine the boy, and the Brāhmaṇa said:"

"If he were to remain a householder, he would receive the rank of a consecrated Wheel-Turning King, ruling over the four continents, endowed with a thousand sons and possessing majestic power and fearlessness; he would be able to subdue enemy armies without the use of weapons, bows, or swords.
Furthermore, if he were to leave the household life and practice with firm resolve, he would attain Perfect Enlightenment."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"The physiognomist brahmin, having divined this celestial youth, addressed his royal father, saying: 'He possesses the thirty-two marks of excellence.'"
Like the moon rising above the multitude of stars, he is most rare in this world.
If he remains forever in his palace, he will surely succeed to the rank of a Wheel-Turning King,
ruling over the four great continents and fathering a thousand princes.
"Thus, at the time of renunciation, one shall swiftly achieve unsurpassed enlightenment.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen now with close attention!"

When that bodhisattva-mahāsattva was born from the right side, his body was of true golden color and his various marks were dignified and majestic; like a lotus born from water, he was unstained by dust or grime, and all sentient beings could never gaze upon him enough.

The sounds he utters are subtle, refined, elegant, and melodious; they are like those of the kalaviṅka bird on the Snowy Mountains, which, having eaten flowers and become intoxicated, produces a voice that is exquisite, wondrous, and clear. Among all sentient beings who hear it, there are none who do not find it delightful; such too are the words and sounds of this youth.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"When the youth was first born, His physical marks were of true golden color,
Like a red lotus flower, Unstained by dust or grime."
"The sound of his voice is most subtle and exquisite, like the call of the kalaviṅka;
when the multitude hears it, they delight in it without ever being satiated.
At that time, having spoken this verse, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"Listen attentively!

When that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva was a youth, he remained far removed from falsehood and delusion, his mind pure and upright. He awakened himself and awakened others, constantly practicing the True Dharma. All people served him, and like Śakra, Lord of the Devas, he honored and revered his parents; for this reason, he was named Vipaśyin."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse: "When Vipaśyin Tathāgata was a youth,
He attained great wisdom And remained far removed from error and delusion."
Awakening oneself and awakening others, practicing the conduct of the True Dharma,
one is always loved and respected by all, like that Śakra-devānām-indra.
By serving and supporting one's parents, one’s fame fills the world.
"He is named Vipaśyin, who brings benefit to all sentient beings.
— *The Sūtra on the Seven Buddhas Spoken by the Buddha*
